1	# Trilayer stacking identification from Raman data (ABA vs ABC)
2	
3	*Investigation — reads **supplied** Raman spectra or hyperspectral maps of a
4	trilayer-graphene flake/device and produces a spot-resolved stacking call.
5	This modality is data-analysis, not instrument-driving: the acquisition
6	already happened, usually on another instrument at another time — which is
7	why acquisition metadata and build-stage provenance are load-bearing inputs,
8	not details.*
9	
10	**References**: the three ingested papers ground every claim —
11	`hera/docs/papers/1011.3021/paper.md` (Lui 2011 — 2D lineshape + FWHM
12	mapping), `hera/docs/papers/nn203472f/paper.md` (Cong 2011 — M-band/G-width
13	cross-checks, q = 2k mechanism), `hera/docs/papers/srep04630/paper.md`
14	(Nguyen 2014 — excitation systematics, two-wavelength rule). Extraction
15	tool: `hera/models/raman_stacking/` (validated on labeled public data —
16	see its README for the gates and calibration facts).
17	
18	## What
19	
20	Classify the stacking of trilayer graphene — ABA (Bernal) vs ABC
21	(rhombohedral) — **per spot / per mapped region** from Raman data, chiefly
22	the 2D-band lineshape. Output is a region-resolved, evidence-cited, hedged,
23	**stage-stamped** call: Raman evidence is about the flake *at map time*, not
24	about the device after subsequent processing.
25	
26	## When
27	
28	- Raman data for the flake/device exists (fabrication screening, a
29	  collaborator's characterization) and stacking bears on the science.
30	- As the second modality against a transport stacking call
31	  (`stacking-raman-transport-fusion.md` consumes this recipe's output).
32	- Prerequisite: none on the rig — this runs from files. Prerequisite on
33	  the data: acquisition metadata (Step 0). Data lacking metadata supports
34	  at most weak calls.
35	
36	## Why
37	
38	The 2D (G′) band is a double-resonance process sampling the electronic
39	bands near K; stacking changes those bands, which changes the resonant
40	phonon wavevectors (q ≈ 2k, larger in ABC — Cong, paper-data). Phonon
41	frequencies themselves are stacking-blind (Γ differences ≤ 0.2 cm⁻¹), so
42	**the contrast is electronic** and rides on the band structure — the same
43	physics transport reads, seen optically.
44	
45	Discriminators, by strength (each with confounds inline):
46	
47	- **2D-band width + lineshape (primary).** ABC: broader (single-Lorentzian
48	  FWHM), asymmetric, sharp peak + enhanced shoulder; ABA: narrower,
49	  smoother (Lui Fig. 2; validated on labeled public data — magnitudes in
50	  the tool README's gate table, not quoted here). Split the axes:
51	  *presence* of a broad population is weak alone; a *pattern* — bimodal
52	  FWHM populations forming spatially coherent domains with sharp walls —
53	  is strong; *magnitude* of the split (≳ 10 cm⁻¹ between population
54	  means, heuristic from the labeled sets) calibrates confidence. When
55	  pattern and magnitude disagree — coherent bimodal domains below the
56	  magnitude heuristic — the pattern sets the grade and the split size
57	  becomes a named hedge.
58	  **Confounds**: uniaxial strain broadens *and* asymmetrizes the 2D
59	  exactly like the ABC signature (0.1–0.2% suffices; strain shifts run
60	  −60…−140 cm⁻¹/% — citation, Mohiuddin PRB 79 205433 / Zabel NL 12 617);
61	  doping/disorder broaden (Lui: chemically processed samples can lose the
62	  contrast); **layer number raises FWHM** (validated: ABC 67→80 cm⁻¹ over
63	  N = 3–10), so a terrace step mimics a stacking wall; low-twist
64	  reconstructed t(1+2) presents a broad asymmetric 2D (citation, Gadelha
65	  2DM 9 025007); spectral resolution inflates FWHM (Lui mapped at
66	  8 cm⁻¹); **the probe integrates the whole vertical stack** — on a
67	  gated/finished device, graphite gates and any other graphene in the
68	  spot contribute their own (Bernal-like) 2D weight, and the collected
69	  band is a superposition the single-layer metrics cannot unmix (Verify:
70	  through-stack screen; QC0426 burn, 2026-07-17).
71	- **M band, 1690–2150 cm⁻¹ (secondary cross-check).** One dominant M⁻
72	  peak = ABA-consistent; split/multiple sharp peaks = ABC-consistent;
73	  iTOLA/LOLA ~10 cm⁻¹ blueshifted in ABC (Cong Fig. 2; Nguyen Fig. 3).
74	  **Confounds**: weak modes (needs SNR); assignments muddy near
75	  E_laser ≈ 2.1–2.4 eV (dispersive-mode crossing); prefer red
76	  excitation. At in-zone excitation treat the M read as uninformative —
77	  direction-inverted signatures are expected there, not anomalies.
78	  Practitioner note: lab convention weights the M-band and G-width
79	  channels at ~zero (PI review, 2026-07-17) — they stay here as
80	  *quantitative secondaries* for agent use, never the call.
81	- **G-band width (supporting only).** ABC narrower (Cong Fig. 6,
82	  FWHM(G) maps 18–24 cm⁻¹ window). **Confounds**: strain and doping both
83	  move G; a few-cm⁻¹ effect — confirming channel, never the call.
84	- **Ultra-low-frequency shear modes (decisive when present, rarely
85	  acquired).** ABA: C mode ~33 cm⁻¹, ABC: C′ ~19 cm⁻¹ — symmetry-
86	  forbidden in the other stacking (citation, Lui APL 106 041904;
87	  suspended samples, ULF filters). If the data includes < 50 cm⁻¹
88	  coverage, this alone can settle a spot.
89	- **Non-discriminators**: G position (~1 cm⁻¹ — below strain/doping
90	  systematics), layer-breathing modes (stacking-blind — citation, Lui
91	  APL 106 041904), absolute intensities (substrate interference
92	  modulates them — read widths and shapes, not brightness).
93	
94	Four disciplines keep the read honest:
95	
96	- **Differential, never absolute.** Absolute FWHM folds in instrument
97	  resolution and wavelength; classify by the **differential across one
98	  flake/map** (the two-population split) or against same-instrument
99	  references — Raman is only trustworthy as a differential measurement
100	  on the same flake. A lone spectrum with no reference supports at most
101	  consistent-with.
102	- **Wavelength is metadata.** Lineshape comparisons only at matching
103	  excitation energy; single-wavelength calls are legitimate only with the
104	  layer number independently known (Nguyen's two-wavelength rule).
105	- **Layer count before stacking.** FWHM grows with N; confirm the layer
106	  count (optical contrast / prior characterization) before reading width
107	  as stacking. A thickness terrace inside the map is the first
108	  alternative hypothesis for any "domain wall".
109	- **Per-spot reads; mixed spectra are mixtures.** Domains span any size,
110	  but µm-scale domains are common (Lui: ~40% of trilayers mixed, none
111	  purely ABC), so walls crossing the ~µm spot are the norm: a spot
112	  straddling a wall gives a linear combination (Lui SI), which FWHM
113	  thresholding mis-bins either way; an intermediate-FWHM spectrum with
114	  poor single-Lorentzian fit is a **mixed candidate, not a third
115	  category**. Domains *below* the spot size are invisible outright.
116	
117	**Stage-stamping (the perishability rule).** ABC is the metastable
118	stacking; documented converters: laser heating at the ~10 mW scale
119	(~430 K local; mapping at ≤ 1 mW is safe by an order of magnitude —
120	citation, Zhang LSA 9 174), adsorbate chemistry + modest bake (citation,
121	Zhang NC 4 2074), **anisotropic strain from metal-contact deposition —
122	walls move by µm** (citation, Geisenhof AANM 2 6067), hBN pickup along
123	armchair (zigzag preserves — citation, Yang NL 19 8526). Conversion runs
124	**ABC→ABA only**; spontaneous ABA→ABC during processing is undocumented.
125	Every verdict therefore carries the acquisition stage and the list of
126	subsequent build steps; a pre-fab map constrains the finished device only
127	modulo those steps.
128	
129	**Beyond trilayer (tetralayer+).** The 2D-FWHM discriminator is
130	family-level and validated across N = 3–10 (rhombohedral-family FWHM
131	exceeds Bernal-family at every N, separation growing with N — extraction
132	tool gates A/C, `hera/models/raman_stacking/README.md`); at N = 4 read
133	Bernal (ABAB) vs rhombohedral (ABCA) the same way, with the
134	within-one-map two-population split carrying the classification (Bernal
135	widths are nearly N-flat; rhombohedral widths grow with N, so absolute
136	thresholds transfer even worse across N). Trilayer-specific numbers in
137	this recipe (Lui's mixed-domain statistics, converter list) are N = 3
138	facts; treat the conversion direction — rhombohedral→Bernal only — as
139	the family-level rule. The mixed order ABCB is a two-way-FWHM blind spot
140	[citation, Wirth et al. arXiv:2203.07971 — not ingested]: FWHM alone may
141	not separate ABCB from ABAB (literature discriminates via G-peak
142	position and near-field imaging), so a Bernal-family FWHM call at N = 4
143	cannot exclude ABCB — hedge accordingly.
144	
145	## Recipe
146	
147	**Step 0 — inventory the data and its provenance (binding: produce the
148	table, not an acknowledgement).** For each file: excitation wavelength,
149	laser power, spot size, map step, spectral resolution/grating, raw vs
150	processed (background-subtracted? normalized?), acquisition date, and
151	**build stage** (what fabrication steps preceded the map; which followed
152	it, by risk class — metal deposition / transfer–pickup / chemical+bake /
153	clean thermal). Derived estimates satisfy the table when flagged as such
154	(spot size from objective NA, resolution from grating class); recorded
155	in-fiber power is not at-sample power — treat at-sample as unknown and
156	carry the conversion flag on the in-fiber value. Missing fields cap the
157	achievable strength: no wavelength
158	→ no lineshape comparison against references; no power → flag possible
159	in-measurement conversion if ≥ several mW; no stage → the call cannot be
160	mapped onto the finished device.
161	
162	**Step 1 — layer count.** Establish N independently (optical contrast,
163	AFM, the supplier's characterization). If N is uncertain between 3 and 4,
164	the 2D read inherits that fork (Nguyen: ABC-3L vs ABC-4L needs blue
165	excitation) — report it, don't absorb it.
166	
167	**Step 2 — per-spectrum 2D read.** Run the tool's metrics
168	(`raman_stacking/metrics.py`: single-Lorentzian FWHM, center, skew,
169	low/high ratio, fit r²) on every spectrum. Compare lineshapes against the
170	reference panels **at matching wavelength** (Lui Fig. 2; Nguyen Fig. 1).
171	Low r² with intermediate FWHM → mixed-spectrum candidate (Verify). Skew
172	and low/high ratio are secondary — their sign is excitation-dependent;
173	calibrate direction on the map's own populations, never assume it.
174	
175	**Step 3 — map read (when a map exists).** Per-pixel metrics + junk-fit
176	rejection; **mask thickness populations before the split** (distinct
177	FWHM modes and amplitude steps belonging to other N) — a whole-map
178	split latches onto the thickness contrast and hides the stacking
179	bimodality. Then the two-population split
180	(`raman_stacking/map_tools.py`), trusted only where it is a population
181	structure (separation exceeding within-cluster spread, visible in the
182	histogram) — 2-means returns two clusters on any input, unimodal or
183	junk. Read the *morphology*: spatially
184	coherent clusters with sharp walls = domain pattern (strong); smooth
185	FWHM gradients tracking 2D-position shifts = strain field
186	(consistent-with strain, not ABC); population split co-locating with a
187	thickness terrace = layer-number artifact (uninformative for stacking).
188	Overlay spot/region coordinates on the flake image so the call is
189	spatially addressable downstream.
190	
191	**Step 4 — cross-checks (as the data allows).** M-band region per
192	spectrum (red excitation preferred; away from the 2.1–2.4 eV crossing);
193	FWHM(G) map if G is covered; G-vs-2D position correlation to separate
194	strain from doping trends (citation, Lee NC 3 1024 — monolayer
195	calibration, use directionally). Where two independent channels agree on
196	a region, the verdict strengthens one grade; where they disagree, report
197	the conflict, not the average.
198	
199	**Step 5 — stage-stamp the verdict.** From Step 0's build timeline:
200	verdict is "as of stage S". List post-map steps with their conversion
201	risk. Directionality: post-map processing can only have converted
202	ABC→ABA — a mapped-ABC region may be smaller/absent now; a mapped-ABA
203	region stays ABA (sub-spot ABC slivers and unmapped areas excepted).
204	
205	**Step 6 — the call.** Output contract (all five parts mandatory):
206	
207	1. Per-spot/per-region verdict on the strength scale (decisive / strong /
208	   weak / consistent-with / uninformative), each with its weight word and
209	   stage stamp: `region R (x,y µm, stage S): ABC (strong)`. Ship the
210	   region label mask/raster alongside the prose coordinates — fusion
211	   consumes the raster, and a prose-only region forces a lossy
212	   re-derivation downstream.
213	2. Evidence list: metric values with spectral coordinates (FWHM,
214	   population means, wavelength), the reference panel matched, map
215	   morphology, cross-check outcomes.
216	3. Confidence + named hedges: sub-spot blindness (domains below the spot
217	   size are invisible — this is structural, state it every time),
218	   wavelength coverage, resolution, unmapped areas, layer-count
219	   certainty.
220	4. What would firm it: second wavelength, M-band spectra, higher-res
221	   map, near-field imaging (s-SNOM resolves walls Raman cannot —
222	   citation, Kim ACS Nano 9 6765), or the transport check
223	   (`trilayer-stacking-fs-count.md`).
224	5. **A reasoned "cannot tell" (with the missing metadata or coverage
225	   named) is a successful outcome. A confident call without
226	   feature-level evidence is a protocol violation.**
227	
228	## Verify
229	
230	- **Tool gates current.** `raman_stacking/validate.py` green (all gates;
231	  count and table in the tool README) before trusting metrics on new
232	  data; the gates double as the worked example of every metric.
233	- **Strain-mimic screen (mandatory before any ABC verdict from width
234	  alone).** Broad-FWHM region + smooth spatial gradient + correlated 2D
235	  position shift → consistent-with strain; broad region + bimodal
236	  population + sharp walls + stable 2D position → strong ABC. Uniaxial
237	  strain is the one confound that reproduces both broadening *and*
238	  asymmetry.
239	- **Through-stack screen (mandatory on any post-gate / mid-stack map).**
240	  From the build stage, list every graphene layer in the spot besides
241	  the target (graphite gates, contacts, adjacent flakes). A map taken
242	  **through a graphite gate is weak at best for the buried channel** —
243	  the collected 2D superposes the gate stack's Bernal-like band with the
244	  target's, and the per-spectrum metrics cannot unmix them; cap the
245	  verdict at consistent-with unless the gate contribution is modeled/
246	  subtracted or a pre-gate map exists (which then carries the call).
247	  [heuristic, QC0426 burn 2026-07-17: a post-fab map of a
248	  graphite-gated device read "uniform ABA (strong)" — PI review
249	  identified the signal as substantially the gate stack.]
250	- **Terrace screen.** Any candidate domain wall checked against the
251	  thickness map (optical/AFM); a wall coinciding with a layer step is
252	  uninformative for stacking. Without an external thickness map, in-map
253	  proxies can rule a terrace out: G/2D amplitudes — and the substrate
254	  line (e.g. Si 520 cm⁻¹) where unsaturated — step across a layer
255	  change and match across a stacking wall. **Check the proxy line is
256	  unclipped first**: a saturated line reads as a perfect match
257	  [heuristic, QC0426 flake map 2026-07-25 — Si line saturated, 2D
258	  amplitude carried the screen].
259	- **Twist screen (history-triggered only).** Run when the flake history
260	  suggests it — fold/tear/wrinkle near the region or a transfer anomaly;
261	  fabricated devices rarely warrant it. Trigger: moiré features or a 2D
262	  band decomposable as 1L+2L superposition → twist-contamination fork
263	  (citation, APL 118 133101): report, don't refine.
264	- **Mixed-spectrum decomposition.** For straddling candidates, run
265	  `raman_stacking/metrics.decompose_mixed` against the map's own
266	  population means; α in (0.2–0.8) (heuristic) → report as
267	  mixed/boundary, not as either stacking.
268	- **Excitation-transfer ban.** No threshold, reference lineshape, or
269	  skew direction crosses wavelengths; re-anchor on same-wavelength
270	  references or the map's own populations.
271	- **Absence claims cite resolvability.** "No ABC found" requires: map
272	  coverage stated, spot/step vs expected domain scale, power ≤ ~1 mW
273	  (else the measurement itself may have erased domains), pristine
274	  surface (processing broadening obscures contrast — Lui). Otherwise the
275	  outcome is "not resolved", not "absent".
276	
277	## Examples
278	
279	- QC0426 worked example (our-measurement,
280	  `hera/docs/notes/2026-07-17-QC0426-raman-fusion/raman-read/` + the
281	  correction in its README): a grower-supplied WITec project read
282	  end-to-end via `load_wip`. The read called uniform ABA (strong);
283	  **PI review identified the map as substantially probing the graphite
284	  gate stack** (post-fab device, graphite gates — Bernal-like 2D from
285	  the gates superposed on the channel's), and the verdict was downgraded
286	  to consistent-with — the burn that produced the through-stack screen
287	  (Verify). Mechanical lessons that stand: one of two scans proved
288	  partial *and* defocused (caught by Step 0 + per-pixel quality metrics);
289	  the single Spot spectrum landed on bare substrate (uninformative).
290	  Stage lesson: imagery-inferred stage stamps (both agents') were
291	  settled only by the grower — carry them as hedged inferences, never
292	  as established metadata.
293	
294	- QC0426 pre-fab ladder (our-measurement,
295	  `hera/docs/notes/2026-07-25-QC0426-prefab-raman/`): maps of the same
296	  device at three build stages (flake / stack / finished device). Only
297	  the flake-stage map is gate-clean — graphite enters at the stack
298	  stage, so the through-stack screen triggers mid-ladder. Also the
299	  worked case for masking thickness populations before the split, the
300	  bimodality gate, and proxy-saturation checking (the flake map's Si
301	  line is clipped). Read details live in the note's contract.
302	
303	- The FLG_37 mixed-flake map (labeled public data, 488 nm): per-pixel
304	  FWHM + two-population split resolved 60 vs 78 cm⁻¹ populations as
305	  spatially coherent domains with sharp walls; cluster means matched the
306	  deposit's labeled region averages to ~1 cm⁻¹
307	  (`hera/models/raman_stacking/README.md`, `flg37_map_validation.png`).
308	  Also the worked case for the layer-number discipline: the flake's 7-
309	  and 8-layer terraces carry distinct FWHM baselines.
310	- Metric calibration facts (which metrics are robust, which directions
311	  flip) live in the tool README's validation table — consult before
312	  weighting skew/ratio evidence.
313	
314	## Next
315	
316	- **Feeding fusion**: hand this contract's per-region verdicts to
317	  `stacking-raman-transport-fusion.md` for reconciliation with a
318	  transport call on the same device.
319	- **ABC-positive regions**: if the device/science depends on them,
320	  near-field imaging or the transport check before committing fridge
321	  time — Raman cannot see sub-spot structure or post-map conversion.
322	- **Ambiguous/strained/mixed**: the transport FS-count is the in-situ
323	  arbiter on the finished device; price it rather than re-arguing the
324	  same Raman data.

Four disciplines keep the read honest:

- **Differential, never absolute.** Absolute FWHM folds in instrument
  resolution and wavelength; classify by the **differential across one
  flake/map** (the two-population split) or against same-instrument
  references — Raman is only trustworthy as a differential measurement
  on the same flake. A lone spectrum with no reference supports at most
  consistent-with.
- **Wavelength is metadata.** Lineshape comparisons only at matching
  excitation energy; single-wavelength calls are legitimate only with the
  layer number independently known (Nguyen's two-wavelength rule).
- **Layer count before stacking.** FWHM grows with N; confirm the layer
  count (optical contrast / prior characterization) before reading width
  as stacking. A thickness terrace inside the map is the first
  alternative hypothesis for any "domain wall".
- **Per-spot reads; mixed spectra are mixtures.** Domains span any size,
  but µm-scale domains are common (Lui: ~40% of trilayers mixed, none
  purely ABC), so walls crossing the ~µm spot are the norm: a spot
  straddling a wall gives a linear combination (Lui SI), which FWHM
  thresholding mis-bins either way; an intermediate-FWHM spectrum with
  poor single-Lorentzian fit is a **mixed candidate, not a third
  category**. Domains *below* the spot size are invisible outright.

**Stage-stamping (the perishability rule).** ABC is the metastable
stacking; documented converters: laser heating at the ~10 mW scale
(~430 K local; mapping at ≤ 1 mW is safe by an order of magnitude —
citation, Zhang LSA 9 174), adsorbate chemistry + modest bake (citation,
Zhang NC 4 2074), **anisotropic strain from metal-contact deposition —
walls move by µm** (citation, Geisenhof AANM 2 6067), hBN pickup along
armchair (zigzag preserves — citation, Yang NL 19 8526). Conversion runs
**ABC→ABA only**; spontaneous ABA→ABC during processing is undocumented.
Every verdict therefore carries the acquisition stage and the list of
subsequent build steps; a pre-fab map constrains the finished device only
modulo those steps.

**Beyond trilayer (tetralayer+).** The 2D-FWHM discriminator is
family-level and validated across N = 3–10 (rhombohedral-family FWHM
exceeds Bernal-family at every N, separation growing with N — extraction
tool gates A/C, `hera/models/raman_stacking/README.md`); at N = 4 read
Bernal (ABAB) vs rhombohedral (ABCA) the same way, with the
within-one-map two-population split carrying the classification (Bernal
widths are nearly N-flat; rhombohedral widths grow with N, so absolute
thresholds transfer even worse across N). Trilayer-specific numbers in
this recipe (Lui's mixed-domain statistics, converter list) are N = 3
facts; treat the conversion direction — rhombohedral→Bernal only — as
the family-level rule. The mixed order ABCB is a two-way-FWHM blind spot
[citation, Wirth et al. arXiv:2203.07971 — not ingested]: FWHM alone may
not separate ABCB from ABAB (literature discriminates via G-peak
position and near-field imaging), so a Bernal-family FWHM call at N = 4
cannot exclude ABCB — hedge accordingly.

## Recipe

**Step 0 — inventory the data and its provenance (binding: produce the
table, not an acknowledgement).** For each file: excitation wavelength,
laser power, spot size, map step, spectral resolution/grating, raw vs
processed (background-subtracted? normalized?), acquisition date, and
**build stage** (what fabrication steps preceded the map; which followed
it, by risk class — metal deposition / transfer–pickup / chemical+bake /
clean thermal). Derived estimates satisfy the table when flagged as such
(spot size from objective NA, resolution from grating class); recorded
in-fiber power is not at-sample power — treat at-sample as unknown and
carry the conversion flag on the in-fiber value. Missing fields cap the
achievable strength: no wavelength
→ no lineshape comparison against references; no power → flag possible
in-measurement conversion if ≥ several mW; no stage → the call cannot be
mapped onto the finished device.

**Step 1 — layer count.** Establish N independently (optical contrast,
AFM, the supplier's characterization). If N is uncertain between 3 and 4,
the 2D read inherits that fork (Nguyen: ABC-3L vs ABC-4L needs blue
excitation) — report it, don't absorb it.

**Step 2 — per-spectrum 2D read.** Run the tool's metrics
(`raman_stacking/metrics.py`: single-Lorentzian FWHM, center, skew,
low/high ratio, fit r²) on every spectrum. Compare lineshapes against the
reference panels **at matching wavelength** (Lui Fig. 2; Nguyen Fig. 1).
Low r² with intermediate FWHM → mixed-spectrum candidate (Verify). Skew
and low/high ratio are secondary — their sign is excitation-dependent;
calibrate direction on the map's own populations, never assume it.

**Step 3 — map read (when a map exists).** Per-pixel metrics + junk-fit
rejection; **mask thickness populations before the split** (distinct
FWHM modes and amplitude steps belonging to other N) — a whole-map
split latches onto the thickness contrast and hides the stacking
bimodality. Then the two-population split
(`raman_stacking/map_tools.py`), trusted only where it is a population
structure (separation exceeding within-cluster spread, visible in the
histogram) — 2-means returns two clusters on any input, unimodal or
junk. Read the *morphology*: spatially
coherent clusters with sharp walls = domain pattern (strong); smooth
FWHM gradients tracking 2D-position shifts = strain field
(consistent-with strain, not ABC); population split co-locating with a
thickness terrace = layer-number artifact (uninformative for stacking).
Overlay spot/region coordinates on the flake image so the call is
spatially addressable downstream.

**Step 4 — cross-checks (as the data allows).** M-band region per
spectrum (red excitation preferred; away from the 2.1–2.4 eV crossing);
FWHM(G) map if G is covered; G-vs-2D position correlation to separate
strain from doping trends (citation, Lee NC 3 1024 — monolayer
calibration, use directionally). Where two independent channels agree on
a region, the verdict strengthens one grade; where they disagree, report
the conflict, not the average.

**Step 5 — stage-stamp the verdict.** From Step 0's build timeline:
verdict is "as of stage S". List post-map steps with their conversion
risk. Directionality: post-map processing can only have converted
ABC→ABA — a mapped-ABC region may be smaller/absent now; a mapped-ABA
region stays ABA (sub-spot ABC slivers and unmapped areas excepted).

**Step 6 — the call.** Output contract (all five parts mandatory):

1. Per-spot/per-region verdict on the strength scale (decisive / strong /
   weak / consistent-with / uninformative), each with its weight word and
   stage stamp: `region R (x,y µm, stage S): ABC (strong)`. Ship the
   region label mask/raster alongside the prose coordinates — fusion
   consumes the raster, and a prose-only region forces a lossy
   re-derivation downstream.
2. Evidence list: metric values with spectral coordinates (FWHM,
   population means, wavelength), the reference panel matched, map
   morphology, cross-check outcomes.
3. Confidence + named hedges: sub-spot blindness (domains below the spot
   size are invisible — this is structural, state it every time),
   wavelength coverage, resolution, unmapped areas, layer-count
   certainty.
4. What would firm it: second wavelength, M-band spectra, higher-res
   map, near-field imaging (s-SNOM resolves walls Raman cannot —
   citation, Kim ACS Nano 9 6765), or the transport check
   (`trilayer-stacking-fs-count.md`).
5. **A reasoned "cannot tell" (with the missing metadata or coverage
   named) is a successful outcome. A confident call without
   feature-level evidence is a protocol violation.**

## Verify

- **Tool gates current.** `raman_stacking/validate.py` green (all gates;
  count and table in the tool README) before trusting metrics on new
  data; the gates double as the worked example of every metric.
- **Strain-mimic screen (mandatory before any ABC verdict from width
  alone).** Broad-FWHM region + smooth spatial gradient + correlated 2D
  position shift → consistent-with strain; broad region + bimodal
  population + sharp walls + stable 2D position → strong ABC. Uniaxial
  strain is the one confound that reproduces both broadening *and*
  asymmetry.
- **Through-stack screen (mandatory on any post-gate / mid-stack map).**
  From the build stage, list every graphene layer in the spot besides
  the target (graphite gates, contacts, adjacent flakes). A map taken
  **through a graphite gate is weak at best for the buried channel** —
  the collected 2D superposes the gate stack's Bernal-like band with the
  target's, and the per-spectrum metrics cannot unmix them; cap the
  verdict at consistent-with unless the gate contribution is modeled/
  subtracted or a pre-gate map exists (which then carries the call).
  [heuristic, QC0426 burn 2026-07-17: a post-fab map of a
  graphite-gated device read "uniform ABA (strong)" — PI review
  identified the signal as substantially the gate stack.]
- **Terrace screen.** Any candidate domain wall checked against the
  thickness map (optical/AFM); a wall coinciding with a layer step is
  uninformative for stacking. Without an external thickness map, in-map
  proxies can rule a terrace out: G/2D amplitudes — and the substrate
  line (e.g. Si 520 cm⁻¹) where unsaturated — step across a layer
  change and match across a stacking wall. **Check the proxy line is
  unclipped first**: a saturated line reads as a perfect match
  [heuristic, QC0426 flake map 2026-07-25 — Si line saturated, 2D
  amplitude carried the screen].
- **Twist screen (history-triggered only).** Run when the flake history
  suggests it — fold/tear/wrinkle near the region or a transfer anomaly;
  fabricated devices rarely warrant it. Trigger: moiré features or a 2D
  band decomposable as 1L+2L superposition → twist-contamination fork
  (citation, APL 118 133101): report, don't refine.
- **Mixed-spectrum decomposition.** For straddling candidates, run
  `raman_stacking/metrics.decompose_mixed` against the map's own
  population means; α in (0.2–0.8) (heuristic) → report as
  mixed/boundary, not as either stacking.
- **Excitation-transfer ban.** No threshold, reference lineshape, or
  skew direction crosses wavelengths; re-anchor on same-wavelength
  references or the map's own populations.
- **Absence claims cite resolvability.** "No ABC found" requires: map
  coverage stated, spot/step vs expected domain scale, power ≤ ~1 mW
  (else the measurement itself may have erased domains), pristine
  surface (processing broadening obscures contrast — Lui). Otherwise the
  outcome is "not resolved", not "absent".

## Examples

- QC0426 worked example (our-measurement,
  `hera/docs/notes/2026-07-17-QC0426-raman-fusion/raman-read/` + the
  correction in its README): a grower-supplied WITec project read
  end-to-end via `load_wip`. The read called uniform ABA (strong);
  **PI review identified the map as substantially probing the graphite
  gate stack** (post-fab device, graphite gates — Bernal-like 2D from
  the gates superposed on the channel's), and the verdict was downgraded
  to consistent-with — the burn that produced the through-stack screen
  (Verify). Mechanical lessons that stand: one of two scans proved
  partial *and* defocused (caught by Step 0 + per-pixel quality metrics);
  the single Spot spectrum landed on bare substrate (uninformative).
  Stage lesson: imagery-inferred stage stamps (both agents') were
  settled only by the grower — carry them as hedged inferences, never
  as established metadata.

- QC0426 pre-fab ladder (our-measurement,
  `hera/docs/notes/2026-07-25-QC0426-prefab-raman/`): maps of the same
  device at three build stages (flake / stack / finished device). Only
  the flake-stage map is gate-clean — graphite enters at the stack
  stage, so the through-stack screen triggers mid-ladder. Also the
  worked case for masking thickness populations before the split, the
  bimodality gate, and proxy-saturation checking (the flake map's Si
  line is clipped). Read details live in the note's contract.

- The FLG_37 mixed-flake map (labeled public data, 488 nm): per-pixel
  FWHM + two-population split resolved 60 vs 78 cm⁻¹ populations as
  spatially coherent domains with sharp walls; cluster means matched the
  deposit's labeled region averages to ~1 cm⁻¹
  (`hera/models/raman_stacking/README.md`, `flg37_map_validation.png`).
  Also the worked case for the layer-number discipline: the flake's 7-
  and 8-layer terraces carry distinct FWHM baselines.
- Metric calibration facts (which metrics are robust, which directions
  flip) live in the tool README's validation table — consult before
  weighting skew/ratio evidence.

## Next

- **Feeding fusion**: hand this contract's per-region verdicts to
  `stacking-raman-transport-fusion.md` for reconciliation with a
  transport call on the same device.
- **ABC-positive regions**: if the device/science depends on them,
  near-field imaging or the transport check before committing fridge
  time — Raman cannot see sub-spot structure or post-map conversion.
- **Ambiguous/strained/mixed**: the transport FS-count is the in-situ
  arbiter on the finished device; price it rather than re-arguing the
  same Raman data.

# raman_stacking — 2D-band metrics + map segmentation for stacking reads

Extraction tool backing `recipes/investigations/raman-stacking-id.md`: computes
the standard stacking-discriminating Raman metrics from supplied spectra or
hyperspectral maps, and segments a map into candidate stacking populations.
This is an **extraction/metric tool, not a forward model** — no double-resonance
lineshape is computed; reference lineshapes come from labeled public data.

## Files

| File | What it does |
|---|---|
| `raman_io.py` | Loaders: WITec ASCII exports (spectra + maps), **WITec `.wip` project files** (`load_wip`, optional `witio` package — also exposes the in-file video images + µm grids for registration), headerless two-column, PKU interleaved CSV. Data root `$HERA_DATA/raman-public-data`. |
| `metrics.py` | Per-spectrum 2D-band metrics (single-Lorentzian FWHM, center, moment skew, low/high-side ratio, fit r²) + G-band position/FWHM + `decompose_mixed()` (α-fit of a spectrum against two same-instrument reference means — the boundary/mixed-pixel read). All 2D metrics are **center-relative** — absolute windows don't transfer across excitation wavelengths (2D disperses ~100 cm⁻¹/eV). |
| `map_tools.py` | Per-pixel metrics with junk-fit rejection (SNR, FWHM ∈ 15–200 cm⁻¹, r² > 0.4), two-population 1-D 2-means split, cluster mean spectra. |
| `validate.py` | The validation gates below. Re-run after any metric change. |
| `flg37_map_validation.png` | Worked map overlay (gate D output). |

Run: `uv run --no-project --with numpy --with scipy --with matplotlib python3 validate.py`

## Validation — gated on labeled public data (2026-07-17, 7/7 pass)

Datasets in `$HERA_DATA/raman-public-data/` (`hera/docs/raman-public-data.md`):
Zenodo 20374368 (PKU, CC-BY 4.0) and Zenodo 10931524 (Nemes-Incze group,
CC-BY-SA 4.0).

| Gate | Data | Result |
|---|---|---|
| A | PKU labeled ABC-vs-AB spectra, N = 3–10, 200 | FWHM(ABC) > FWHM(AB) at every N; **trilayer: 67.1 vs 63.2 cm⁻¹**; separation grows with N (10 L: 80.3 vs 63.9) |
| B | Nemes labeled single pair (hexa vs rhomb) | rhomb 80.7 vs hexa 64.0 cm⁻¹ |
| C | 29 labeled-ABC spectra, 488/532/633 nm | FWHM 72–92 cm⁻¹ across all three wavelengths (4–12 L) |
| D | Nemes FLG_37 hyperspectral map (488 nm, 48×45 px) | two-population split at 60.2 / 77.9 cm⁻¹; cluster-mean FWHM 62.0 / 77.9 vs labeled region averages hexa 60.6–60.9 / rhomb 78.1–78.6; domains spatially coherent with sharp walls |
| E | synthetic mixtures of gate D's cluster means (2% noise) | `decompose_mixed` recovers α = 0–1 within ±0.1; 78% of the map's real intermediate-FWHM pixels decompose at α ∈ (0.2, 0.8) — wall mixtures, not a third phase |

Validation-derived calibration facts (this data, not universal):

- **FWHM is the workhorse metric.** Clean separation in every gate. The
  asymmetry metrics (moment skew, low/high-side ratio) are **weak and
  direction-inconsistent** across datasets/excitations here — e.g. PKU AB
  spectra show a *higher* low/high ratio than ABC. Treat asymmetry as a
  secondary, locally calibrated check, never the call. (Consistent with Lui
  et al. 2011 settling on FWHM for imaging.)
- **Absolute FWHM values do not transfer** between instruments (spectral
  resolution folds in) — classify by the two-population split within one
  map/flake, or against same-instrument references, never by a universal
  threshold.
- **Layer number also raises 2D FWHM** (PKU: ABC 67→80 cm⁻¹ over N = 3–10).
  A two-population split on a multi-thickness flake confounds thickness with
  stacking — interpret clusters against the thickness map.

## Caveats / assumptions

- **PKU label assumption (flagged):** Figure4A/2C1 = ABC, Figure4B/2C2 = AB —
  inferred from the deposit's ABC-first column convention and lineshapes

  cm⁻¹, their flat-band identification method) — public trilayer 2D-band
  truth rests on the PKU set. Map gate D is a 7/8-layer flake: it validates
  the pipeline, not trilayer specifically.

  spectra**; the deposit has no per-pixel masks).

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""
3	Loaders for Raman spectra / hyperspectral maps used by the raman_stacking tool.
4	
5	Supported formats:
6	  - WITec ASCII export ("//Exported ASCII-File" + [Header] + [Data]):
7	    single spectra (2 cols) and maps (1 + SizeX*SizeY cols, column (x/y) order).
8	  - Headerless two-column whitespace text (wavenumber, counts).
9	  - PKU Zenodo-20374368 interleaved CSV: repeated (shift, intensity) column
10	    pairs, one pair per labeled trace.
11	
12	Public data root: $HERA_DATA/raman-public-data (default /data/sharpelab/hera-data).
13	"""
14	import csv
15	import os
16	import re
17	from pathlib import Path
18	
19	import numpy as np
20	
21	
22	def data_root():
23	    return Path(os.environ.get("HERA_DATA", "/data/sharpelab/hera-data")) / "raman-public-data"
24	
25	
26	def _parse_witec_header(lines):
27	    hdr = {}
28	    for ln in lines:
29	        if "=" in ln:
30	            k, v = ln.split("=", 1)
31	            hdr[k.strip()] = v.strip()
32	    return hdr
33	
34	
35	def load_witec(path):
36	    """WITec ASCII export -> (wavenumber[n], intensity[n, ncols], header dict).
37	
38	    Single spectra come back with ncols == 1. Map pixel columns are in the
39	    export's (x/y) order: column index j -> x = j % SizeX, y = j // SizeX.
40	    """
41	    path = Path(path)
42	    raw = path.read_text(errors="replace").splitlines()
43	    try:
44	        i_data = next(i for i, ln in enumerate(raw) if ln.strip() == "[Data]")
45	    except StopIteration:
46	        raise ValueError(f"no [Data] section in {path}")
47	    hdr = _parse_witec_header(raw[:i_data])
48	    rows = []
49	    for ln in raw[i_data + 1:]:
50	        parts = ln.split("\t")
51	        try:
52	            rows.append([float(p) for p in parts])
53	        except ValueError:
54	            continue  # X-Axis / unit label lines
55	    arr = np.array(rows)
56	    order = np.argsort(arr[:, 0])
57	    return arr[order, 0], arr[order, 1:], hdr
58

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Loaders for Raman spectra / hyperspectral maps used by the raman_stacking tool.

Supported formats:
  - WITec ASCII export ("//Exported ASCII-File" + [Header] + [Data]):
    single spectra (2 cols) and maps (1 + SizeX*SizeY cols, column (x/y) order).
  - Headerless two-column whitespace text (wavenumber, counts).
  - PKU Zenodo-20374368 interleaved CSV: repeated (shift, intensity) column
    pairs, one pair per labeled trace.

Public data root: $HERA_DATA/raman-public-data (default /data/sharpelab/hera-data).
"""
import csv
import os
import re
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np


def data_root():
    return Path(os.environ.get("HERA_DATA", "/data/sharpelab/hera-data")) / "raman-public-data"


def _parse_witec_header(lines):
    hdr = {}
    for ln in lines:
        if "=" in ln:
            k, v = ln.split("=", 1)
            hdr[k.strip()] = v.strip()
    return hdr


def load_witec(path):
    """WITec ASCII export -> (wavenumber[n], intensity[n, ncols], header dict).

    Single spectra come back with ncols == 1. Map pixel columns are in the
    export's (x/y) order: column index j -> x = j % SizeX, y = j // SizeX.
    """
    path = Path(path)
    raw = path.read_text(errors="replace").splitlines()
    try:
        i_data = next(i for i, ln in enumerate(raw) if ln.strip() == "[Data]")
    except StopIteration:
        raise ValueError(f"no [Data] section in {path}")
    hdr = _parse_witec_header(raw[:i_data])
    rows = []
    for ln in raw[i_data + 1:]:
        parts = ln.split("\t")
        try:
            rows.append([float(p) for p in parts])
        except ValueError:
            continue  # X-Axis / unit label lines
    arr = np.array(rows)
    order = np.argsort(arr[:, 0])
    return arr[order, 0], arr[order, 1:], hdr


def load_two_column(path):
    """Headerless whitespace two-column text -> (wavenumber, intensity)."""
    arr = np.loadtxt(path)
    order = np.argsort(arr[:, 0])
    return arr[order, 0], arr[order, 1]


def load_spectrum(path):
    """Sniff format; return (wavenumber, intensity) for a single spectrum."""
    with open(path, errors="replace") as f:
        first = f.readline()
    if first.startswith("//Exported"):
        wn, ii, _ = load_witec(path)
        return wn, ii[:, 0]
    return load_two_column(path)


def witec_excitation_nm(info_path):
    """Excitation wavelength from a WITec --Information.txt file, else None."""
    text = Path(info_path).read_text(errors="replace")
    m = re.search(r"Excitation Wavelength \[nm\]:\s*([\d.]+)", text)
    return float(m.group(1)) if m else None


def map_shape(hdr):
    return int(hdr["SizeX"]), int(hdr["SizeY"])


def load_wip(path):
    """WITec Project (.wip) -> list of spectral datasets, via the optional
    `witio` package (`uv run --with witio ...`).

    Each returned dict: caption, wn (ascending cm^-1), ii[n_wn, ncols]
    (map columns x-fastest, matching load_witec: x = j % nx), nx, ny, meta
    (the WITec measurement metadata dict — wavelength, power-in-fiber,
    integration time, scan geometry, timestamps). Non-spectral project
    items (video images, cursors, transformations) are skipped; read them
    with witio directly if needed (video images carry per-pixel µm grids
    for registration).
    """
    import witio  # optional dep

    out = []
    for d in witio.read(str(path)).data:
        try:
            arr = d.array()
            xa = d.x_axis()
        except Exception:
            continue
        arr = np.asarray(arr)
        meta = d.measurement_metadata
        meta = meta() if callable(meta) else meta
        meta = meta or {}
        if arr.ndim == 3:            # hyperspectral map
            # witio yields (x, y, n_spec) when the in-file scan_size
            # metadata matches (shape[0], shape[1]); transpose so the
            # column order is x-fastest with nx/ny in the sample frame.
            sx = meta.get("scan_size_x_px")
            sy = meta.get("scan_size_y_px")
            if sx and sy and (int(sx), int(sy)) == arr.shape[:2]:
                arr = arr.transpose(1, 0, 2)
            ny, nx, nsp = arr.shape
            ii = arr.reshape(ny * nx, nsp).T
        elif arr.ndim == 1:          # single spectrum
            ny, nx = 1, 1
            ii = arr[:, None]
        else:
            continue
        wn = np.asarray(xa[0] if isinstance(xa, tuple) else xa,
                        dtype=float).ravel()
        if wn.size != ii.shape[0]:
            continue
        order = np.argsort(wn)
        out.append(dict(caption=d.caption, wn=wn[order], ii=ii[order],
                        nx=nx, ny=ny, meta=meta))
    return out


def load_pku_pairs(path):
    """PKU interleaved CSV -> list of (label, wavenumber, intensity)."""
    with open(path, encoding="utf-8-sig") as f:
        rows = list(csv.reader(f))
    heads = rows[0]
    out = []
    for j in range(0, len(heads), 2):
        label = heads[j + 1]
        wn, ii = [], []
        for r in rows[1:]:
            if j + 1 < len(r) and r[j] and r[j + 1]:
                wn.append(float(r[j]))
                ii.append(float(r[j + 1]))
        wn, ii = np.array(wn), np.array(ii)
        order = np.argsort(wn)
        out.append((label, wn[order], ii[order]))
    return out

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
2D-band (and G-band) metrics for graphene stacking reads.

All 2D metrics are computed about the *fitted* 2D center, never absolute
wavenumber windows: the 2D band disperses ~100 cm^-1/eV with excitation
energy, so absolute windows calibrated at one wavelength do not transfer.

Metrics (per spectrum):
  fwhm      single-Lorentzian FWHM of the whole 2D band -- the workhorse
            map metric (Lui et al. 2011). ABC broader than ABA.
  skew      intensity-weighted third moment in center +/- HALF cm^-1.
            ABC's asymmetric shoulder gives it a sign; direction is
            established empirically by validate.py, not assumed.
  ratio_lh  integrated low-side / high-side intensity about the center
            (center-relative version of the Yang et al. 2019 window ratio).
  center    fitted 2D peak position (cm^-1).
  r2        Lorentzian fit quality; low r2 = structured band (multi-peak /
            mixed spectrum), itself information.

No external deps beyond numpy/scipy.
"""
import numpy as np
from scipy.optimize import curve_fit

TWO_D_SEARCH = (2550.0, 2850.0)  # 2D peak search window, generous across 1.9-2.8 eV
FIT_HALF = 150.0                 # Lorentzian fit half-window about the peak
HALF = 100.0                     # moment/ratio half-window
G_SEARCH = (1500.0, 1650.0)


def _lorentz(x, a, x0, w, c):
    return a * (w / 2) ** 2 / ((x - x0) ** 2 + (w / 2) ** 2) + c


def _clip(wn, ii, lo, hi):
    m = (wn >= lo) & (wn <= hi)
    return wn[m], ii[m]


def fit_band(wn, ii, search, fit_half=FIT_HALF):
    """Single Lorentzian + const in a window about the band maximum.

    Returns dict(center, fwhm, amp, offset, r2) or None if the band is
    absent / fit fails.
    """
    w, i = _clip(wn, ii, *search)
    f = np.isfinite(i)
    w, i = w[f], i[f]          # partial maps carry all-NaN columns
    if len(w) < 10:
        return None
    x0 = w[np.argmax(i)]
    w, i = _clip(wn, ii, x0 - fit_half, x0 + fit_half)
    if len(w) < 10:
        return None
    base = np.median(np.concatenate([i[:5], i[-5:]]))
    amp0 = i.max() - base
    if amp0 <= 0:
        return None
    try:
        p, _ = curve_fit(_lorentz, w, i, p0=[amp0, x0, 40.0, base],
                         maxfev=5000)
    except RuntimeError:
        return None
    a, x0f, fw, c = p
    fw = abs(fw)
    resid = i - _lorentz(w, *p)
    ss_tot = np.sum((i - i.mean()) ** 2)
    r2 = 1 - np.sum(resid ** 2) / ss_tot if ss_tot > 0 else 0.0
    if not (search[0] - 50 < x0f < search[1] + 50) or fw > 400:
        return None
    return dict(center=x0f, fwhm=fw, amp=a, offset=c, r2=r2)


def metrics_2d(wn, ii):
    """2D-band metric set for one spectrum, or None if no usable 2D band."""
    fit = fit_band(wn, ii, TWO_D_SEARCH)
    if fit is None or fit["amp"] <= 0:
        return None
    c = fit["center"]
    w, i = _clip(wn, ii, c - HALF, c + HALF)
    if len(w) < 10:
        return None
    i = i - fit["offset"]
    i = np.clip(i, 0, None)
    tot = np.trapezoid(i, w)
    if tot <= 0:
        return None
    mu = np.trapezoid(i * w, w) / tot
    var = np.trapezoid(i * (w - mu) ** 2, w) / tot
    skew = (np.trapezoid(i * (w - mu) ** 3, w) / tot) / var ** 1.5 if var > 0 else 0.0
    lo_m = (w >= c - HALF) & (w <= c - 10)
    hi_m = (w >= c + 10) & (w <= c + HALF)
    lo = np.trapezoid(i[lo_m], w[lo_m]) if lo_m.sum() > 1 else 0.0
    hi = np.trapezoid(i[hi_m], w[hi_m]) if hi_m.sum() > 1 else 0.0
    ratio = lo / hi if hi > 0 else np.inf
    return dict(center=fit["center"], fwhm=fit["fwhm"], amp=fit["amp"],
                r2=fit["r2"], skew=skew, ratio_lh=ratio)


def decompose_mixed(wn, spec, ref_a, ref_b, window=(2550.0, 2850.0)):
    """Fit spec ≈ α·ref_a + (1−α)·ref_b (all on the same wavenumber grid,
    area-normalized in `window`). The references should be same-instrument,
    same-wavelength population means (e.g. a map's own cluster means).

    Returns dict(alpha, r2): alpha = weight of ref_a, clipped to [0, 1];
    r2 = fit quality (low r2 → the spectrum is not a two-component mixture
    of these references). None if the window is empty or a ref is degenerate.
    """
    m = (wn >= window[0]) & (wn <= window[1])
    if m.sum() < 20:
        return None

    def norm(y):
        yy = np.clip(y[m], 0, None)
        a = np.trapezoid(yy, wn[m])
        return yy / a if a > 0 else None

    s, a, b = norm(spec), norm(ref_a), norm(ref_b)
    if s is None or a is None or b is None:
        return None
    d = a - b
    denom = float(d @ d)
    if denom <= 0:
        return None
    alpha = float(np.clip((s - b) @ d / denom, 0.0, 1.0))
    fit = alpha * a + (1 - alpha) * b
    ss_tot = float(((s - s.mean()) ** 2).sum())
    r2 = 1 - float(((s - fit) ** 2).sum()) / ss_tot if ss_tot > 0 else 0.0
    return dict(alpha=alpha, r2=r2)


def metrics_g(wn, ii):
    """G-band position/FWHM (needs the spectrum to cover ~1500-1650)."""
    if wn.min() > G_SEARCH[0]:
        return None
    fit = fit_band(wn, ii, G_SEARCH, fit_half=60.0)
    if fit is None:
        return None
    return dict(center=fit["center"], fwhm=fit["fwhm"], r2=fit["r2"])

2	"""
3	Hyperspectral-map tools: per-pixel 2D metrics + two-population segmentation.
4	
5	Segmentation is *relative* (two populations within one map), never an
6	absolute FWHM threshold: absolute thresholds fold in instrument resolution
7	and excitation wavelength and do not transfer between setups. Layer-number
8	steps also shift 2D FWHM, so a two-population split on a multi-thickness
9	flake is a first pass, not a verdict -- interpret clusters against the
10	flake's thickness map.
11	
12	No external deps beyond numpy/scipy (matplotlib only for save_maps).
13	"""
14	import numpy as np
15	
16	from metrics import metrics_2d
17	
18	METRIC_KEYS = ("center", "fwhm", "amp", "r2", "skew", "ratio_lh")
19	
20	
21	def per_pixel_metrics(wn, ii, min_amp_snr=8.0):
22	    """Metric arrays over map columns; NaN where no credible 2D band.
23	
24	    min_amp_snr: peak amplitude must exceed this multiple of the per-pixel
25	    noise floor (median |diff|) -- excludes substrate / dead pixels.
26	    """
27	    n = ii.shape[1]
28	    out = {k: np.full(n, np.nan) for k in METRIC_KEYS}
29	    for j in range(n):
30	        y = ii[:, j]
31	        noise = np.median(np.abs(np.diff(y))) + 1e-12
32	        m = metrics_2d(wn, y)
33	        if m is None or m["amp"] < min_amp_snr * noise:

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Hyperspectral-map tools: per-pixel 2D metrics + two-population segmentation.

Segmentation is *relative* (two populations within one map), never an
absolute FWHM threshold: absolute thresholds fold in instrument resolution
and excitation wavelength and do not transfer between setups. Layer-number
steps also shift 2D FWHM, so a two-population split on a multi-thickness
flake is a first pass, not a verdict -- interpret clusters against the
flake's thickness map.

No external deps beyond numpy/scipy (matplotlib only for save_maps).
"""
import numpy as np

from metrics import metrics_2d

METRIC_KEYS = ("center", "fwhm", "amp", "r2", "skew", "ratio_lh")


def per_pixel_metrics(wn, ii, min_amp_snr=8.0):
    """Metric arrays over map columns; NaN where no credible 2D band.

    min_amp_snr: peak amplitude must exceed this multiple of the per-pixel
    noise floor (median |diff|) -- excludes substrate / dead pixels.
    """
    n = ii.shape[1]
    out = {k: np.full(n, np.nan) for k in METRIC_KEYS}
    for j in range(n):
        y = ii[:, j]
        noise = np.median(np.abs(np.diff(y))) + 1e-12
        m = metrics_2d(wn, y)
        if m is None or m["amp"] < min_amp_snr * noise:
            continue
        if not (15.0 < m["fwhm"] < 200.0) or m["r2"] < 0.4:
            continue  # spike/junk fit, not a graphene 2D band
        for k in METRIC_KEYS:
            out[k][j] = m[k]
    return out


def two_population_split(values, n_iter=50):
    """1-D 2-means. Returns (labels 0/1 with 1 = higher-mean cluster, centers).

    NaNs stay unlabeled (-1).
    """
    v = np.asarray(values, float)
    ok = np.isfinite(v)
    labels = np.full(v.shape, -1, int)
    if ok.sum() < 4:
        return labels, (np.nan, np.nan)
    lo, hi = np.percentile(v[ok], [10, 90])
    c = np.array([lo, hi], float)
    for _ in range(n_iter):
        d = np.abs(v[ok, None] - c[None, :])
        lab = d.argmin(axis=1)
        new = np.array([v[ok][lab == k].mean() if (lab == k).any() else c[k]
                        for k in (0, 1)])
        if np.allclose(new, c):
            break
        c = new
    if c[0] > c[1]:
        c = c[::-1]
        lab = 1 - lab
    labels[ok] = lab
    return labels, tuple(c)


def to_image(vec, size_x, size_y):
    """Map-column vector -> (size_y, size_x) image (row-major x-fastest)."""
    return np.asarray(vec).reshape(size_y, size_x)


def cluster_mean_spectrum(ii, labels, k):
    """Mean spectrum over map columns with label k."""
    sel = labels == k
    return ii[:, sel].mean(axis=1) if sel.any() else None

107	def gate_c_nemes_layers():
108	    d = data_root() / "zenodo-10931524-nemes" / "Figure 3 and 4" / "data"
109	    rows, ers_only = [], []
110	    for sub in sorted(d.iterdir()):

133	    print("  dir              file                                      nm     FWHM   skew")
134	    for name, fn, nm, mm in rows:
135	        print(f"  {name:<16} {fn:<40} {nm:6.0f} {mm['fwhm']:7.1f} {mm['skew']:6.2f}")
136	    for name, lo, hi in ers_only:

148

150	def gate_d_map():

152	    matplotlib.use("Agg")
153	    import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
154	
155	    base = data_root() / "zenodo-10931524-nemes"
156	    wn, ii, hdr = load_witec(
157	        base / "Figure 2" /

183	    # correlation is dominated by overall band presence and cannot
184	    # separate 61 vs 78 cm^-1 populations.
185	    match, ok_match = {}, True

206	        spec = cluster_mean_spectrum(ii, labels, k)
207	        axes[2].plot(wn, spec / spec.max(), color,
208	                     label=f"cluster {k} ({'narrow' if k == 0 else 'broad'})")
209	    for tag, sty in (("hexa-7L", "C0--"), ("rhomb-7L", "C3--")):
210	        rwn, rii, _ = refs[tag]
211	        rn = rii - np.median(rii[:50])
212	        axes[2].plot(rwn, rn / rn.max(), sty, alpha=0.6, label=f"ref {tag}")

223	def gate_e_decompose(wn, ii, px, labels):
224	    """Mixed-spectrum decomposition: recover known synthetic mixing

228	    b = cluster_mean_spectrum(ii, labels, 1)  # broad / rhomb
229	    rng = np.random.default_rng(20260717)
230	    noise = 0.02 * b.max()
231	    ok, rows = True, []
232	    for alpha_true in (0.0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0):
233	        s = alpha_true * a + (1 - alpha_true) * b + rng.normal(0, noise, a.shape)
234	        d = decompose_mixed(wn, s, a, b)
235	        rows.append((alpha_true, d["alpha"], d["r2"]))

239	    inter = np.where((px["fwhm"] > 65) & (px["fwhm"] < 73))[0]
240	    alphas = [decompose_mixed(wn, ii[:, j], a, b)["alpha"] for j in inter]
241	    frac_mid = np.mean([(0.2 < al < 0.8) for al in alphas]) if alphas else 0.0
242	    print(f"  {len(inter)} intermediate-FWHM map pixels: "
243	          f"{100*frac_mid:.0f}% decompose at α ∈ (0.2, 0.8)")

257	    return 1 if fails else 0

"""
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np

from raman_io import (data_root, load_pku_pairs, load_spectrum, load_witec,
                      map_shape, witec_excitation_nm)
from metrics import decompose_mixed, metrics_2d
from map_tools import (cluster_mean_spectrum, per_pixel_metrics, to_image,

OUT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
RESULTS = []


def report(gate, ok, msg):
    RESULTS.append((gate, ok, msg))

def gate_a_pku():
    d = data_root() / "zenodo-20374368-pku"

        (_, wn, ii), = load_pku_pairs(d / f)
        pair.append(metrics_2d(wn, ii))
    report("A.pku-fig2c", pair[0]["fwhm"] > pair[1]["fwhm"],
           f"2C1 (ABC-labeled) FWHM {pair[0]['fwhm']:.1f} vs 2C2 {pair[1]['fwhm']:.1f}")
    return {n: (m_abc[n], m_ab[n]) for n in shared}


def gate_b_nemes_pair():
    d = data_root() / "zenodo-10931524-nemes" / "Figure 2"
    wn_h, i_h = load_spectrum(d / "FLG_38--Spectrum--045--Spec.Data 1_ss_hexa.txt")
    wn_r, i_r = load_spectrum(d / "FLG_38--Spectrum--046--Spec.Data 1_ss_rhomb.txt")
    mh, mr = metrics_2d(wn_h, i_h), metrics_2d(wn_r, i_r)
    report("B.nemes-pair", mr["fwhm"] > mh["fwhm"],
           f"rhomb FWHM {mr['fwhm']:.1f} / skew {mr['skew']:.2f} vs "
           f"hexa {mh['fwhm']:.1f} / {mh['skew']:.2f}")
    return mh, mr


def gate_c_nemes_layers():
    d = data_root() / "zenodo-10931524-nemes" / "Figure 3 and 4" / "data"
    rows, ers_only = [], []
    for sub in sorted(d.iterdir()):
        if not sub.is_dir() or "layer" not in sub.name:
            continue
        nm = None
        for info in sub.glob("*Information.txt"):
            nm = witec_excitation_nm(info)
            if nm:
                break
        if nm is None:
            m = re.search(r"_(\d{3})$", sub.name)
            nm = float(m.group(1)) if m else np.nan
        for f in sorted(sub.glob("*.txt")):
            if "Information" in f.name:
                continue
            try:
                wn, ii = load_spectrum(f)
            except Exception:
                continue
            mm = metrics_2d(wn, ii)
            if mm:
                rows.append((sub.name, f.name[:40], nm, mm))
            else:
                ers_only.append((sub.name, wn.min(), wn.max()))
    print("  dir              file                                      nm     FWHM   skew")
    for name, fn, nm, mm in rows:
        print(f"  {name:<16} {fn:<40} {nm:6.0f} {mm['fwhm']:7.1f} {mm['skew']:6.2f}")
    for name, lo, hi in ers_only:
        print(f"  {name:<16} [ERS-region export, {lo:.0f}-{hi:.0f} cm^-1, no 2D band]")
    wavelengths = {round(nm) for _, _, nm, _ in rows if np.isfinite(nm)}
    fwhms = np.array([mm["fwhm"] for _, _, _, mm in rows])
    skews = np.array([mm["skew"] for _, _, _, mm in rows])
    ok = len(rows) >= 10 and len(wavelengths) >= 2
    report("C.nemes-abc-layers", ok,
           f"{len(rows)} labeled-ABC 2D spectra at {sorted(wavelengths)} nm, "
           f"FWHM {fwhms.min():.0f}-{fwhms.max():.0f}, median skew {np.median(skews):.2f}; "
           f"{len(ers_only)} ERS-only exports (incl. all trilayer -- 2D-band "
           f"trilayer truth is Gate A)")
    return rows


def gate_d_map():
    import matplotlib
    matplotlib.use("Agg")
    import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

    base = data_root() / "zenodo-10931524-nemes"
    wn, ii, hdr = load_witec(
        base / "Figure 2" /
        "FLG_37--Scan Piezo--013--Spec.Data 1 (Sub BG) (CRR)_2D only_anal90.txt")
    sx, sy = map_shape(hdr)
    px = per_pixel_metrics(wn, ii)
    labels, centers = two_population_split(px["fwhm"])
    n0, n1 = (labels == 0).sum(), (labels == 1).sum()
    print(f"  map {sx}x{sy}: {np.isfinite(px['fwhm']).sum()} graphene px, "
          f"clusters {n0} @ {centers[0]:.1f} / {n1} @ {centers[1]:.1f} cm^-1")

    # labeled region-average spectra from the deposit (7/8-layer hexa/rhomb)
    refs = {}
    rdir = base / "Figure 3 and 4"
    for f in rdir.glob("*mask_Draw Image*"):
        tag = ("rhomb" if "rhom" in f.name else "hexa") + \
              ("-7L" if f.name.startswith("7") else "-8L")
        rwn, rii = load_spectrum(f)
        refs[tag] = (rwn, rii, metrics_2d(rwn, rii))
    for tag, (_, _, m) in sorted(refs.items()):
        print(f"  ref {tag:<9} FWHM {m['fwhm']:6.1f}  skew {m['skew']:5.2f}")
    ok_refs = all(refs[f"rhomb-{n}"][2]["fwhm"] > refs[f"hexa-{n}"][2]["fwhm"]
                  for n in ("7L", "8L"))
    report("D.map-refs", ok_refs,
           "labeled region averages: rhomb FWHM > hexa at 7L and 8L")

    # Match each cluster to the labeled averages by the discriminating
    # metric itself (FWHM of the cluster-mean spectrum): waveform
    # correlation is dominated by overall band presence and cannot
    # separate 61 vs 78 cm^-1 populations.
    match, ok_match = {}, True
    for k, want in ((0, "hexa"), (1, "rhomb")):
        spec = cluster_mean_spectrum(ii, labels, k)
        mm = metrics_2d(wn, spec)
        best = min(refs, key=lambda t: abs(refs[t][2]["fwhm"] - mm["fwhm"]))
        match[k] = (best, mm["fwhm"])
        ok_match &= best.startswith(want)
        print(f"  cluster {k} ({'low' if k == 0 else 'high'}-FWHM) mean-spectrum "
              f"FWHM {mm['fwhm']:.1f} -> nearest ref {best} "
              f"({refs[best][2]['fwhm']:.1f})")
    report("D.map-clusters", ok_match,
           f"low-FWHM cluster -> {match[0][0]}, high-FWHM cluster -> {match[1][0]}")

    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(14, 4))
    im0 = axes[0].imshow(to_image(px["fwhm"], sx, sy), origin="lower", cmap="viridis")
    axes[0].set_title("2D FWHM (cm$^{-1}$)")
    fig.colorbar(im0, ax=axes[0], shrink=0.8)
    axes[1].imshow(to_image(labels, sx, sy), origin="lower", cmap="coolwarm",
                   vmin=-1, vmax=1)
    axes[1].set_title(f"segmentation (red=broad, {centers[1]:.0f} cm$^{{-1}}$)")
    for k, color in ((0, "C0"), (1, "C3")):
        spec = cluster_mean_spectrum(ii, labels, k)
        axes[2].plot(wn, spec / spec.max(), color,
                     label=f"cluster {k} ({'narrow' if k == 0 else 'broad'})")
    for tag, sty in (("hexa-7L", "C0--"), ("rhomb-7L", "C3--")):
        rwn, rii, _ = refs[tag]
        rn = rii - np.median(rii[:50])
        axes[2].plot(rwn, rn / rn.max(), sty, alpha=0.6, label=f"ref {tag}")
    axes[2].set_xlim(2550, 2850)
    axes[2].set_xlabel("Raman shift (cm$^{-1}$)")
    axes[2].legend(fontsize=7)
    axes[2].set_title("cluster means vs labeled averages")
    fig.tight_layout()
    fig.savefig(OUT / "flg37_map_validation.png", dpi=140)
    print(f"  wrote {OUT / 'flg37_map_validation.png'}")
    return wn, ii, px, labels


def gate_e_decompose(wn, ii, px, labels):
    """Mixed-spectrum decomposition: recover known synthetic mixing
    fractions of the map's own cluster means (small noise added), and
    report the α distribution of the real intermediate-FWHM pixels."""
    a = cluster_mean_spectrum(ii, labels, 0)  # narrow / hexa
    b = cluster_mean_spectrum(ii, labels, 1)  # broad / rhomb
    rng = np.random.default_rng(20260717)
    noise = 0.02 * b.max()
    ok, rows = True, []
    for alpha_true in (0.0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0):
        s = alpha_true * a + (1 - alpha_true) * b + rng.normal(0, noise, a.shape)
        d = decompose_mixed(wn, s, a, b)
        rows.append((alpha_true, d["alpha"], d["r2"]))
        ok &= abs(d["alpha"] - alpha_true) < 0.1
    for at, af, r2 in rows:
        print(f"  synthetic α={at:.2f} -> recovered {af:.3f} (r2 {r2:.3f})")
    inter = np.where((px["fwhm"] > 65) & (px["fwhm"] < 73))[0]
    alphas = [decompose_mixed(wn, ii[:, j], a, b)["alpha"] for j in inter]
    frac_mid = np.mean([(0.2 < al < 0.8) for al in alphas]) if alphas else 0.0
    print(f"  {len(inter)} intermediate-FWHM map pixels: "
          f"{100*frac_mid:.0f}% decompose at α ∈ (0.2, 0.8)")
    report("E.decompose", ok,
           f"synthetic mixtures recovered within ±0.1 at 2% noise "
           f"(real wall pixels: {100*frac_mid:.0f}% mid-α)")


def main():
    gate_a_pku()
    gate_b_nemes_pair()
    gate_c_nemes_layers()
    gate_e_decompose(*gate_d_map())
    print()
    fails = [r for r in RESULTS if not r[1]]
    print(f"{len(RESULTS) - len(fails)}/{len(RESULTS)} gates passed")
    return 1 if fails else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Step 1 aux — export the three video images with stage-µm extents, the
two fast-scan intensity images, and the two Raman maps' mean spectra.
Registration only; no stacking metrics here."""
from pathlib import Path

import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import witio

HERE = Path(__file__).parent
proj = witio.read(str(HERE / "inputs" / "vti-01.wip"))
items = {k: d for k, d in enumerate(proj.data)}


def tag_child(tag, *names):
    t = tag
    for n in names:
        t = next(c for c in t.children if c.name == n)
    return t


def transform_params(d):
    vp = tag_child(d.payload, "ViewPort3D")
    origin = tag_child(vp, "WorldOrigin").data
    scale = tag_child(vp, "Scale").data.reshape(3, 3)
    rot = tag_child(vp, "Rotation").data.reshape(3, 3)
    model = tag_child(vp, "ModelOrigin").data
    return model, origin, scale, rot


def px_to_world(model, origin, scale, rot, px, py):
    v = np.stack([px - model[0], py - model[1], np.zeros_like(px)], -1)
    return (rot @ (scale @ v[..., None]))[..., :2, 0] + origin[:2]


# bitmap -> its transformation item index
BM = {19: 18, 24: 23, 32: 31}
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(19, 6))
for ax, (kb, kt) in zip(axes, BM.items()):
    img = np.asarray(items[kb].array())
    model, origin, scale, rot = transform_params(items[kt])
    ny, nx = img.shape[1], img.shape[0]
    # witio bitmap array is (W, H, 3)? report both and use corners
    W, H = img.shape[0], img.shape[1]
    corners = px_to_world(model, origin, scale, rot,
                          np.array([0.0, W, W, 0.0]), np.array([0.0, 0.0, H, H]))
    print(f"item {kb}: {items[kb].caption} array {img.shape} corners:\n{corners}")
    ext = [corners[:, 0].min(), corners[:, 0].max(),
           corners[:, 1].min(), corners[:, 1].max()]
    # display: transpose to (H, W, 3); y axis decreasing scale -> origin upper
    ax.imshow(img.transpose(1, 0, 2) if img.shape[0] > img.shape[1] else img,
              extent=ext, origin="upper")
    ax.set_title(items[kb].caption, fontsize=9)
    ax.set_xlabel("stage x (µm)")
axes[0].set_ylabel("stage y (µm)")
# overlay scan footprints on each
scans = {22: ("map A (532)", "w"), 27: ("map B (532)", "y"),
         30: ("006 fast", "c"), 35: ("008 fast", "m")}
for ax in axes:
    for ks, (lab, col) in scans.items():
        meta = items[ks].measurement_metadata
        meta = meta() if callable(meta) else meta
        cx, cy = meta["scan_center_x_um"], meta["scan_center_y_um"]
        sx, sy = meta["scan_span_x_um"], meta["scan_span_y_um"]
        ax.add_patch(plt.Rectangle((cx - sx / 2, cy - sy / 2), sx, sy,
                                   fill=False, ec=col, lw=1.2))
        ax.annotate(lab, (cx - sx / 2, cy + sy / 2), color=col, fontsize=7)
fig.tight_layout()
fig.savefig(HERE / "fig_video_images.png", dpi=130)
print("wrote fig_video_images.png")

# fast scans as total-intensity images + Raman map mean spectra
fig2, axes2 = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(13, 9))
for ax, ks in zip(axes2[0], (30, 35)):
    d = items[ks]
    arr = np.asarray(d.array())  # (?, ?, nspec)
    tot = arr.sum(axis=-1)
    meta = d.measurement_metadata
    meta = meta() if callable(meta) else meta
    sx, sy = meta["scan_size_x_px"], meta["scan_size_y_px"]
    print(f"item {ks}: {d.caption} arr {arr.shape} scan_size ({sx},{sy})")
    if tot.shape == (sx, sy):
        tot = tot.T
    cx, cy = meta["scan_center_x_um"], meta["scan_center_y_um"]
    wx, wy = meta["scan_span_x_um"], meta["scan_span_y_um"]
    ax.imshow(tot, extent=[cx - wx/2, cx + wx/2, cy - wy/2, cy + wy/2],
              origin="lower", cmap="gray")
    ax.set_title(f"{d.caption} total counts")
for ax, ks in zip(axes2[1], (22, 27)):
    d = items[ks]
    arr = np.asarray(d.array())
    xa = d.x_axis()
    wn = np.asarray(xa[0] if isinstance(xa, tuple) else xa, float).ravel()
    mean = arr.reshape(-1, arr.shape[-1]).mean(axis=0)
    order = np.argsort(wn)
    ax.plot(wn[order], mean[order], lw=0.7)
    ax.set_title(f"{d.caption} mean spectrum")
    ax.set_xlabel("rel. cm$^{-1}$")
    print(f"item {ks}: wn {wn.min():.1f}..{wn.max():.1f}, "
          f"mean counts min {mean.min():.0f} max {mean.max():.0f}")
fig2.tight_layout()
fig2.savefig(HERE / "fig_firstlook.png", dpi=130)
print("wrote fig_firstlook.png")

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Step 2/3 — per-pixel metrics for maps A (Scan 003) and B (Scan 005):
2D metrics (tool), G metrics, Si-520 amplitude (terrace proxy), raw-count
ceiling (saturation check). Saves map_metrics.npz + overview figures."""
import sys
from pathlib import Path

HERE = Path(__file__).parent
sys.path.insert(0, str(HERE / "tools"))

import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

from raman_io import load_wip
from metrics import fit_band, metrics_g
from map_tools import per_pixel_metrics, to_image, METRIC_KEYS

dsets = load_wip(HERE / "inputs" / "vti-01.wip")
maps = {d["caption"]: d for d in dsets}
A = maps["73474_--Scan LA--003--Spec.Data 1"]
B = maps["73474_--Scan LA--005--Spec.Data 1"]

out = {}
for tag, d in (("A", A), ("B", B)):
    wn, ii, nx, ny = d["wn"], d["ii"], d["nx"], d["ny"]
    meta = d["meta"]
    print(f"map {tag}: {nx}x{ny}, center ({meta['scan_center_x_um']:.1f}, "
          f"{meta['scan_center_y_um']:.1f}), span {meta['scan_span_x_um']}x"
          f"{meta['scan_span_y_um']} µm")
    px = per_pixel_metrics(wn, ii)
    n = ii.shape[1]
    g_center = np.full(n, np.nan); g_fwhm = np.full(n, np.nan)
    g_amp = np.full(n, np.nan); si_amp = np.full(n, np.nan)
    raw_max = np.full(n, np.nan)
    for j in range(n):
        y = ii[:, j]
        raw_max[j] = np.nanmax(y)
        g = metrics_g(wn, y)
        if g is not None:
            g_center[j], g_fwhm[j] = g["center"], g["fwhm"]
        gf = fit_band(wn, y, (1500.0, 1650.0), fit_half=60.0)
        if gf is not None:
            g_amp[j] = gf["amp"]
        sf = fit_band(wn, y, (490.0, 550.0), fit_half=40.0)
        if sf is not None and 500 < sf["center"] < 540:
            si_amp[j] = sf["amp"]
    out[tag] = dict(px=px, g_center=g_center, g_fwhm=g_fwhm, g_amp=g_amp,
                    si_amp=si_amp, raw_max=raw_max, nx=nx, ny=ny,
                    cx=meta["scan_center_x_um"], cy=meta["scan_center_y_um"],
                    step=meta["scan_span_x_um"] / nx)
    print(f"  graphene px (2D ok): {np.isfinite(px['fwhm']).sum()}/{n}")
    print(f"  raw counts max over map: {np.nanmax(raw_max):.0f} "
          f"(16-bit ceiling 65535); Si amp range "
          f"{np.nanmin(si_amp):.0f}..{np.nanmax(si_amp):.0f}")

np.savez(HERE / "map_metrics.npz",
         **{f"{t}_{k}": v[k] if False else v[k]
            for t, v in out.items() for k in
            ("g_center", "g_fwhm", "g_amp", "si_amp", "raw_max")},
         **{f"{t}_px_{k}": out[t]["px"][k] for t in out for k in METRIC_KEYS},
         A_geom=np.array([out["A"]["cx"], out["A"]["cy"], out["A"]["nx"],
                          out["A"]["ny"], out["A"]["step"]]),
         B_geom=np.array([out["B"]["cx"], out["B"]["cy"], out["B"]["nx"],
                          out["B"]["ny"], out["B"]["step"]]))
print("wrote map_metrics.npz")


def extent(v):
    hx = v["nx"] * v["step"] / 2; hy = v["ny"] * v["step"] / 2
    return [v["cx"] - hx, v["cx"] + hx, v["cy"] - hy, v["cy"] + hy]


for tag, v in out.items():
    nx, ny = v["nx"], v["ny"]
    ext = extent(v)
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 4, figsize=(20, 8))
    panels = [("2D FWHM", v["px"]["fwhm"], "viridis"),
              ("2D center", v["px"]["center"], "coolwarm"),
              ("2D amp", v["px"]["amp"], "magma"),
              ("2D fit r2", v["px"]["r2"], "cividis"),
              ("G center", v["g_center"], "coolwarm"),
              ("G FWHM", v["g_fwhm"], "viridis"),
              ("G amp", v["g_amp"], "magma"),
              ("Si-520 amp", v["si_amp"], "gray")]
    for ax, (title, vec, cmap) in zip(axes.ravel(), panels):
        img = to_image(vec, nx, ny)
        im = ax.imshow(img, extent=ext, origin="upper", cmap=cmap)
        ax.set_title(f"{tag}: {title}")
        fig.colorbar(im, ax=ax, shrink=0.8)
    fig.tight_layout()
    fig.savefig(HERE / f"fig_map{tag}_metrics.png", dpi=120)
    print(f"wrote fig_map{tag}_metrics.png")

# histograms of 2D FWHM
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(12, 4))
for ax, (tag, v) in zip(axes, out.items()):
    f = v["px"]["fwhm"]
    ax.hist(f[np.isfinite(f)], bins=60)
    ax.set_title(f"map {tag}: 2D FWHM histogram")
    ax.set_xlabel("FWHM (cm$^{-1}$)")
fig.tight_layout()
fig.savefig(HERE / "fig_fwhm_hist.png", dpi=120)
print("wrote fig_fwhm_hist.png")

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Step 3 — two-population read on map A (+ map B), with the mandatory
screens: thickness proxies (Si-520 amp, 2D amp, G integral), strain
(2D-center co-variation), morphology (coherent domains vs gradients),
and cross-map consistency A vs B."""
import sys
from pathlib import Path

HERE = Path(__file__).parent
sys.path.insert(0, str(HERE / "tools"))

import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
from scipy import ndimage

from raman_io import load_wip
from map_tools import two_population_split, to_image, cluster_mean_spectrum
from metrics import metrics_2d, decompose_mixed

z = np.load(HERE / "map_metrics.npz")
dsets = load_wip(HERE / "inputs" / "vti-01.wip")
maps = {d["caption"][-15:]: d for d in dsets}
A = maps["003--Spec.Data 1"]
B = maps["005--Spec.Data 1"]


def geom(tag):
    cx, cy, nx, ny, step = z[f"{tag}_geom"]
    return cx, cy, int(nx), int(ny), step


def world_grids(tag):
    cx, cy, nx, ny, step = geom(tag)
    ix = np.arange(nx); iy = np.arange(ny)
    xs = cx + (ix - (nx - 1) / 2.0) * step
    ys = cy - (iy - (ny - 1) / 2.0) * step   # row 0 = +y (Scale y = -1)
    return xs, ys


def g_integral(wn, ii):
    """Integrated G intensity 1565-1605 minus linear baseline from
    1520-1550 / 1620-1650 — robust thickness proxy."""
    def win(lo, hi):
        m = (wn >= lo) & (wn <= hi)
        return m
    mL, mR, mG = win(1520, 1550), win(1620, 1650), win(1565, 1605)
    base = 0.5 * (ii[mL].mean(0) + ii[mR].mean(0))
    return np.clip(ii[mG] - base, 0, None).sum(0)


# ---------- map A ----------
cxA, cyA, nxA, nyA, stepA = geom("A")
fw = z["A_px_fwhm"]; cen = z["A_px_center"]; amp = z["A_px_amp"]
r2 = z["A_px_r2"]; si = z["A_si_amp"]; gfw = z["A_g_fwhm"]; gc = z["A_g_center"]
gint = g_integral(A["wn"], A["ii"])
ok = np.isfinite(fw)
print(f"map A: {ok.sum()} graphene px")

# thickness proxies on flake pixels
print("Si amp on-flake: p5..p95 =", np.nanpercentile(si[ok], [5, 50, 95]).round(0))
print("2D amp on-flake: p5..p95 =", np.nanpercentile(amp[ok], [5, 50, 95]).round(0))
print("G integral on-flake: p5..p95 =", np.nanpercentile(gint[ok], [5, 50, 95]).round(0))

# FWHM split on all flake pixels (first pass)
lab, cent = two_population_split(fw)
print(f"first-pass split: {(lab==0).sum()} @ {cent[0]:.1f} / "
      f"{(lab==1).sum()} @ {cent[1]:.1f} cm^-1")
for k in (0, 1):
    s = lab == k
    print(f"  cluster {k}: FWHM {np.nanmean(fw[s]):.1f}±{np.nanstd(fw[s]):.1f}, "
          f"2D center {np.nanmean(cen[s]):.1f}±{np.nanstd(cen[s]):.1f}, "
          f"2D amp {np.nanmean(amp[s]):.0f}±{np.nanstd(amp[s]):.0f}, "
          f"Si amp {np.nanmean(si[s]):.0f}±{np.nanstd(si[s]):.0f}, "
          f"G int {np.nanmean(gint[s]):.0f}±{np.nanstd(gint[s]):.0f}, "
          f"G FWHM {np.nanmean(gfw[s]):.1f}±{np.nanstd(gfw[s]):.1f}, "
          f"G center {np.nanmean(gc[s]):.2f}±{np.nanstd(gc[s]):.2f}")
sep = cent[1] - cent[0]
w0, w1 = np.nanstd(fw[lab == 0]), np.nanstd(fw[lab == 1])
print(f"separation {sep:.1f} vs within-cluster spread {w0:.1f}/{w1:.1f} "
      f"-> ratio {sep / max(w0, w1):.1f}")

# fold detection: Si amp far below median (thicker), or 2D amp outlier
si_med = np.nanmedian(si[ok])
fold = ok & (si < 0.8 * si_med)
print(f"fold/thick candidate px (Si amp < 0.8*median): {fold.sum()}")
print(f"  their FWHM {np.nanmean(fw[fold]):.1f}, 2D amp {np.nanmean(amp[fold]):.0f}, "
      f"G int {np.nanmean(gint[fold]):.0f}")

# morphology: connected components of the broad cluster (excluding fold)
img_lab = to_image(lab, nxA, nyA).astype(float)
img_fold = to_image(fold, nxA, nyA)
broad = (img_lab == 1) & ~img_fold
narrow = (img_lab == 0) & ~img_fold
for name, m in (("broad", broad), ("narrow", narrow)):
    cc, n = ndimage.label(m)
    sizes = np.sort(np.bincount(cc.ravel())[1:])[::-1]
    print(f"{name}: {n} components, sizes {sizes[:6]}")

# wall sharpness: FWHM profile along rows crossing the main boundary
img_fw = to_image(fw, nxA, nyA)
img_cen = to_image(cen, nxA, nyA)

# strain screen: correlation of FWHM with 2D center among flake px (no fold)
sel = ok & ~fold
cc_fc = np.corrcoef(fw[sel], cen[sel])[0, 1]
cc_fsi = np.corrcoef(fw[sel], si[sel])[0, 1]
cc_famp = np.corrcoef(fw[sel], amp[sel])[0, 1]
cc_fg = np.corrcoef(fw[sel & np.isfinite(gint)], gint[sel & np.isfinite(gint)])[0, 1]
print(f"corr(FWHM, 2D center) = {cc_fc:.2f}")
print(f"corr(FWHM, Si amp)    = {cc_fsi:.2f}")
print(f"corr(FWHM, 2D amp)    = {cc_famp:.2f}")
print(f"corr(FWHM, G int)     = {cc_fg:.2f}")
# per-cluster thickness deltas (excluding fold)
for k in (0, 1):
    s = (lab == k) & ~fold
    print(f"  cluster {k} (no fold): n={s.sum()} Si {np.nanmean(si[s]):.0f} "
          f"2Damp {np.nanmean(amp[s]):.0f} Gint {np.nanmean(gint[s]):.0f} "
          f"2Dcen {np.nanmean(cen[s]):.2f} FWHM {np.nanmean(fw[s]):.2f}")

# G center vs 2D center (strain/doping axis), directional only
s2 = sel & np.isfinite(gc)
print(f"corr(G center, 2D center) = {np.corrcoef(gc[s2], cen[s2])[0,1]:.2f}")

# mixed-spectrum decomposition against A's own cluster means
ref_n = cluster_mean_spectrum(A["ii"], np.where(~fold, lab, -1), 0)
ref_b = cluster_mean_spectrum(A["ii"], np.where(~fold, lab, -1), 1)
mn = metrics_2d(A["wn"], ref_n); mb = metrics_2d(A["wn"], ref_b)
print(f"cluster-mean spectra: narrow FWHM {mn['fwhm']:.1f} r2 {mn['r2']:.3f} "
      f"skew {mn['skew']:.2f} ratio {mn['ratio_lh']:.2f}; "
      f"broad FWHM {mb['fwhm']:.1f} r2 {mb['r2']:.3f} skew {mb['skew']:.2f} "
